rules: The National Polygon Dataset is a subset of the Land Register containing all registered titles relating to land or property.
Index polygons follow MasterMap features where those features relate to the ownership boundary.
Ownership boundaries do not always follow features shown in MasterMap.
Overlaps, gaps, slivers and underlaps exist in the National Polygon dataset.
Many topology imperfections are genuine and acceptable, although some should not exist.
Small technical overlaps caused by mapping inconsistencies do not describe a real conflict of registered titles.
Actual overlaps can occur where multiple titles include the same land and are resolved upon application.
Registrations at different floors, strata, tenures or title classes can create acceptable overlapping polygons.
Caseworkers may classify acceptable overlaps and allow them to remain in the dataset.
Index-polygon overlaps referred by the system are investigated by a caseworker.
Where title extents genuinely overlap, HMLR may take no action until an amendment or rectification application is received.
Overlaps below 0.5 square metres are not referred for remedial action.
Minor index-polygon discrepancies should be resolved where titles are intended to adjoin.
Some registered titles are not intended to adjoin, so their index polygons will not adjoin.
Artificial footprints can divide dense multi-level developments into smaller areas to improve index-map interrogation.
Exaggerated extents use a minimum width of one metre so narrow undefined land can be identified.
Former gridding practice can split one field, house or road at sheet joins into parts with separate polygon IDs.
Former coextensive leasehold indexing was changed because it impeded identification of title numbers for lesser extents.
A change-only delivery contains only the latest polygon version and HMLR does not retain previous versions in that delivery model.

The Planning Data API exposes over 100 planning and housing datasets through one consistent interface.
Latitude and longitude queries return entities whose geometry intersects the supplied point.
Multiple dataset parameters return matching entities from any specified dataset whose geometry covers the point.
Search responses include next, previous, first and last pagination links.
The Planning Data API does not provide a batch endpoint for portfolio screening.
Portfolio screening through the API requires one request per property.
The field parameter can restrict the response to required fields.
The official guide instructs clients to apply polite rate limiting between property requests.
For hundreds of properties or more, bulk downloads and local spatial intersections avoid rate limits and provide a stable snapshot.
Bulk download link URL formats vary by dataset page.

The official 1m composite DTM covers approximately 99 percent of England at one-metre spatial resolution.
The DTM is produced from the last or only laser pulse returned to the sensor.
Surface objects are removed using bespoke algorithms and manual editing to produce a terrain-only model.
The composite combines Time Stamped archive surveys with National LIDAR Programme surveys.
For repeat surveys, the newest best-resolution data is selected.
Bilinear interpolation is used where source data is resampled before merging.
Individual source surveys can range from 25-centimetre to two-metre spatial resolution.
The dataset record exposes survey download, coverage metadata, WMS, WFS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API Features access surfaces.

OS Terrain 50 is updated annually in July.
The product is an open height dataset containing contours, spot heights, breaklines, coastline, lakes, ridges and formlines.
The documented product coverage is Great Britain at a scale of 1:50,000.
The product is maintained through an integrated three-to-five-year flying programme synchronised with other product updates.
The product applies specific modelling to significant height features, particularly networks.
OS Terrain 50 grid data is documented as verified to four-metre RMSE.
OS Terrain 50 is supplied as inert data and does not include data-manipulation software.
